title: Astra medium WSI diagnostic studies
claim: Across five Astra medium diagnostic conditions on four selected public WSI sources, all final answers met the artifact contract, while private references showed partial or uneven task agreement: HuBMAP 86/99 polygons matched, TIGER cell matching mixed with near-perfect attribution only when tissue masks were supplied, CAMELYON 4/6 Tumor polygons hit on one positive slide, and HiESD 3,222/11,290 annotated pixels correct. These are case-specific observations, not comparable population or clinical performance estimates.
limitations: One selected public slide per source, or three fixed TIGER ROIs from one slide, and one stochastic attempt per condition cannot establish population performance, a model ranking or clinical validity; public-data pretraining exposure is unknown.

Harbor reward checks output artifacts rather than scientific correctness. HuBMAP unmatched predictions need annotation-domain review; CAMELYON has no negative or sparse-lesion case; HiESD XML boundaries are coarse and unannotated tissue is not known-normal.

TIGER tissue-supplied compartment accuracy uses the evaluated tissue mask as an input, so its paired contrast is a diagnostic assistance check, not independent tissue inference or a causal detection estimate.
Two earlier Sol attempts and one interrupted Astra transport attempt ended before image analysis and retain no-verdict execution status.

Logged crop containment does not prove focused inspection; native TIFF reads can bypass the helper ledger. TIGER's paired runs used different tile layouts, and post-hoc confidence slices are not validated thresholds.

TIGER's solver prompt omits the scorer's matched-source-center mask convention, affecting two tissue-supplied cells at boundaries. CAMELYON's equal-per-polygon endpoint overweights two tiny polygons close to already-hit tumor regions; 4/6 is not lesion-search sensitivity. HiESD XML covers only 4.0% of its coarse grid. No source GT label defect has been adjudicated.
